videos.title: "I'm Not A TikToker, I'm A Filmmaker" - Gilmore On Streaming, Creativity & His New Chapter
videos.headline: "I'm Not A TikToker, I'm A Filmmaker" - Gilmore On Streaming, Creativity & His New Chapter
videos.description:
Gilmore is leveling up. From TikTok to Twitch. From skits to streaming. And he is bringing the whole culture with him. In this exclusive interview, Gilmore opens up about his transition from short-form content to long-form streaming. He talks about why he is making the switch, what fans can expect, and who he looks up to in the streaming space.

He does not hold back on his favorite streamer. CarterEfe gets the crown. Spontaneous. Versatile. Creative. Painting rooms. Turning studios into beaches. Bringing camels and donkeys into a small space. Gilmore breaks down exactly why CarterEfe is the best in the game right now. And he gives Shank his flowers too. The blueprint is there. The global impact is real. But CarterEfe's consistency and creativity? Unmatched.

He also talks about Peller. Does his success come from being one of the best streamers or from his personality? Gilmore says Peller is super blessed and he is himself. That is the secret.

Gilmore also reveals his next big move. A six-day boarding school stream from the 23rd to the 29th. Costume days. Red nights. Cutting grass. Making Gary cake. Choco bonbon. It is back to back. And he is inviting everyone to tune in on Twitch. He talks about his goals. Slow and steady. Walk-ins. 9mm. No flying. Just climbing step by step. And he predicts a future where Nigerian streamers are on Lamborghinis. Where content creators and streamers become richer than musicians. This is the energy. This is the vision.

videos.title: EXCLUSIVE: Gerard Spills On Araga, Sheba, Chimsom & Why He Didn't "Show Himself" | BBNaija Interview
videos.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Gerard Spills On Araga, Sheba, Chimsom & Why He Didn't "Show Himself" | BBNaija Interview
videos.description:
Gerald is out of the Big Brother Nigeria house and he is spilling everything. From the Araga friendship he wants to keep alive to the Sheba connection he admits could have been something more. From the Chimsom rivalry that rubbed him the wrong way to why viewers felt he did not "show himself" enough. This interview covers it all.

Gerald gets real about his time in the house. He addresses the criticism head on. He knows people wanted drama and romance. He knows they wanted more. But he stayed true to himself. Subtle. Strategic. Focused on showcasing his talents rather than chasing screen time. And he does not apologize for it.

He breaks down the competitive dynamics. Chimsom is a star player but he is all about the win. To hell with feelings. Sheba is a lioness. Strong. Supportive. A girl's girl. And if she was not taken, he admits she would be the one. He also reveals the friendships he wants to carry outside. Araga is a definite. Blue has potential. Everyone else? He is not so sure. The house was a game. Most of it felt like a show.

But Gerald is not just a BBNaija housemate. He is an actor. He played the bad boy pilot on Wings. He played Timmy Sand on Amazon Prime. He is an on-air personality. A poet. A writer. And he is ready for the next chapter. Bigger roles. Brand partnerships. Fashion runways. Spoken word. Love letters. He wants the whole shebang.

videos.title: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.headline: “Burna Boy Is a Huge Inspiration to My Sound” — Buff Opens Up on His Music, 10 Minutes & More
videos.description:
In this exclusive full interview on the Midday Show with Kemi Smalls and Brownish on 96.9 Cool FM, Nigerian artist 6uff (Buff / 6uffzaddy) opens up about his music journey, gym lifestyle, personality, and more.

From church drummer and producer (as Logic) to breakthrough artist, 6uff shares how he started making music in 2021 with “Selfish,” the story behind his stage name, and the impact of family support — especially his mom’s prayers.

He talks about his breakout tracks **Prodigy** and **Idi Amin**, the massive collaboration **10 Minutes** with Odumodublvck, **Ripper’s Fate** with Tuff King, his heavy bass signature sound, perfectionism in the studio, and upcoming projects (including possible links with Burna Boy and Rondtown).

Also covered:

- His 6’5” height and gym dedication (started with homemade cement weights)
- Ambivert personality vs high-energy stage presence and shirtless performances
- Football background (defensive midfield, Barcelona fan)
- Fitness advice, real-life song themes (betrayal, survival, hustle)
- Guilty pleasures, movie preferences, and dream Nigerian cypher line-up

videos.title: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.headline: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.description:
​@LadipoeLOTR  studied Biology and Chemistry at the University of North Carolina before moving back home to Nigeria, hoping to make the big break as a Recording Artist. 

He was in luck. His mother found a kindred spirit: another rapper’s mother while taking a course at the Lagos Business School. That rapper was Wale “Tec” Davies of @showdemcamp. Tec felt his bars and invited him into a creative circle, which incubated acts like Show Dem Camp, Funbi, @temidollfacevevo4701, @temsbaby, and more. 

Poe announced his presence on “Feel Alright”- a collab with SDC and @Bojdrb, which has been credited as being a precursor to the iconic Palm Wine Music series. 

Don Jazzy's @MavinRecords  came calling, and Poe vowed to make the best of the opportunity. Nearly 10 years later, he’s found the type of mainstream appeal that once seemed out of reach. This year, he released "Revival", one of the year’s best releases, highlighting why he’s one of the country’s most beloved artists.  

On this episode of Overnight Success, he takes us on the long journey from medical professional to one of the country's premier rappers.

The multi-talented entertainer opens up on The Beat 99.9 FM about his evolution from viral comedy to serious music production. Breaking the near-impossible stereotype of transitioning from a comedian to a musician in this part of the world, he reveals that music has always been his first love. From building his own studio to making music every single day, he breaks down the process of selecting 15 tracks out of 30 original songs for his debut album, "On Behalf of Josh".

He explains the triple entendre behind the album title, giving fans the "other half" of himself, and details his incredible studio experience learning from rap legend Ice Prince. He also addresses the selfish nature of fans, dealing with negative comments, and why the "2Funny" name will soon be silent. videos.title: La Reezy on New Orleans Hip Hop, Skiddle Bandana & Rap’s Next Generation | The Almanac of Rap
videos.headline: La Reezy on New Orleans Hip Hop, Skiddle Bandana & Rap’s Next Generation | The Almanac of Rap
videos.description:
On this episode of The Almanac of Rap, Donwill heads south to explore the past, present and future of New Orleans hip-hop with rising rapper, producer and 2026 XXL Freshman La Reezy.
La Reezy shares how filming run-and-gun videos around his hometown helped him build an audience outside Louisiana, how a viral streetcar performance caught PJ Morton’s attention, and why he considers himself a “leader of the youth” within a new generation of New Orleans artists. For La Reezy, representing the city isn’t simply an aesthetic, it’s central to his strategy, community and identity.

Fresh off recognition from the National Hip-Hop Museum and an appearance in Kendrick Lamar’s Super Bowl experience, La Reezy also opens up about faith, family, learning from Jon Batiste, studying Kendrick from behind the scenes and his ambitions beyond music. La Reezy breaks down:
- Why representing your hometown can be a competitive advantage
- The streetcar video that caught PJ Morton’s attention
- Performing at Keith Lee’s Family Day
- The ideas behind his debut album, Skiddle Bandana
- His dream of producing for Lil Wayne and NBA YoungBoy
